# Generated endpoint files are named *.cs.cs: decide and document the convention
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #163, sha256:b731b4251ea03f66dcd2b908926c273f9ff51294d2a5bcb0501d9b674af69d20). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** tooling (small; found by the card 160 re-review)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Found 2026-10-28 by the card 160 re-review: the C# adapter names endpoint files like CompleteTask.cs.cs (the file-name helper adds .cs and the caller adds .cs again), since commit 56135ef; acceptance tests already look for the double extension.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want generated files named as ordinary C# files, so that tools, reviewers and analyzers treat the output like any other project.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the C# adapter, When endpoint files are generated, Then each is named <Endpoint>.cs (one extension), the project builds with zero warnings and every existing acceptance test, the README drift test and the Usable v1 bars still pass after their file-name expectations are updated together
  2. Given the generated output of demo/tasks/Tasks.phrase, When it is listed, Then no file ends in .cs.cs and the stored-file naming is covered by one test that fails if the double extension returns
  3. Given docs/adr/ADR-library-binding-layering.md, When the card is merged, Then its audit references to the file-name helper are updated (the checker passes)

## Context

- Cosmetic but visible to every reader of the generated project; the rename touches many tests, so do it in one change.
